messages.subject: data2oscr
parts:
Hello everyone,

 

A few days ago we pushed an update to the data2oSCR() function that fixes an issue when you use the function to generate data for open population SCR (which cannot be fit using oSCR, so this issue does not affect any previous oSCR analyses). The fix now generates capture histories that retain individual identities across sessions (each row in all sessions belong to the same individual) resulting in all-zero encounters in sessions where an individual is not encountered – this is exactly what you need, and previous versions mixed up the ordering.

 

We have now added a check to see if individuals have multiple sexes: if an individual has multiple captures with conflicting sex information and error is thrown. BUT! We noticed that this check is carried out regardless of whether a sex column is included, so would give an error if you are not including sex information. This has now been fixed, so you should reinstall the package as of the 3rd of Feb 2020:

 

remotes::install_github("jaroyle/oSCR")

 

Apologies from the oSCR development team!
